idea: Two-part code head, body paid with the savings
mechanism: Write the loss as a two-stage code: first code the token's frequency cluster (a 384 x 258 head: a 4096-token shortlist plus 2 tail-cluster entries), then code the token inside its cluster against the tied embedding rows of that cluster only. Training computes just the target's cluster, cutting the 42 percent head share of compute to about 4 percent and freeing roughly 1 GB of logits memory; the saved time and memory buy one more block and a modest feed-forward widening, inside the parameter cap. Frequency ranks come from a bincount over 20M train tokens at startup. When targets is None, forwar
prediction: Step time falls to about 3.4 s even with 13 layers; peak VRAM falls by about 0.8 GB; non-embedding params rise to about 23.2M (under 23.37M). Validation loss falls by 0.01 to 0.02 from the extra depth, with a small rise in rare-token loss from the tail clusters.
test: Build-only for the count; 3-step timing and memory; a 45-step matched run; a unit check that exp of the returned full logits sums to one per position and that the two-path cross entropy matches the training loss to 1e-4.
target: loss on rare tokens up slightly; validation loss down overall
scope: validation loss at 1024. New verifier proposed: report loss at matched training wall-clock and a separate column for exa
breaks: The training forward and the exam forward must compute the same dense 50304-wide logits tensor.
keeps: Next-token cross entropy, tied embeddings, the whole body, the optimizer and data path.
kill: At 45 matched steps the training loss is more than 0.08 above the baseline's 45-step loss, or the full-logits path disagrees with the training loss by more than 1e-3.

idea: Second pass over the same rope, different gearing
mechanism: A pulley trades distance for force; here trade the 2x time headroom for depth without new parameters. Run the 12 blocks twice; the second pass shares every matrix but has its own read logits, write logits, mixing logits and norm gains (a few hundred parameters per block), so the same weights act as a different layer by reading and writing different streams. The second pass is activation-checkpointed because memory has only 0.1 GB of headroom.
prediction: Params rise by under 10k; step time rises to roughly 8.5 s with recompute (under 9.53 s); peak VRAM stays within 0.1 GB of today. Loss falls by about 0.02, in line with depth reuse keeping about three quarters of the token efficiency of real depth.
test: 3-step timing and peak-memory check first (this is the likeliest failure); then a 45-step matched run. Falsified if time exceeds 9.5 s or memory exceeds 5.6 GB.
target: residual RMS growth (should stay bounded across 24 applications); validation loss down
scope: validation loss at 1024. New verifier proposed: loss at matched training FLOPs against a FLOP-matched deeper baseline, s
breaks: Each block's parameters are applied exactly once per token per forward.
keeps: Block internals, the 4-stream state, loss and optimizer unchanged; pass 1 is identical to the baseline.
kill: Peak VRAM above 5.6 GB or step above 9.5 s at the 3-step check; otherwise a 45-step loss not at least 0.03 below the baseline's 45-step loss.

idea: Learned cold-start state for the window's first positions
mechanism: The exam cuts 1024-token windows at arbitrary offsets, so the first tens of positions in every window are predicted with almost no context and pay a large, systematic loss that is pure amnesia. Prepend 8 learned soft tokens inside forward (dropped from the logits) that summarise a typical mid-document context; early queries attend to them instead of a single arbitrary first token, which also gives the sink a home.
prediction: Params rise by 3,072; step time rises under 1 percent; loss at positions 0 to 63 falls noticeably while loss at late positions is unchanged, for an average drop of roughly 0.005 to 0.01.
test: A 45-step matched run with the per-position loss logged in 64-token buckets; falsified if the early-position bucket does not drop more than the others. Memory check that 8 extra positions stay under 5.6 GB.
target: first-token attention mass down; loss at late positions unchanged; validation loss down
scope: validation loss at 1024. New verifier proposed: loss reported per position bucket, since a model that only fixes amnesia
breaks: The first token of a window is predicted from an empty context.
keeps: Causal attention, the same windows, the same head; the soft tokens never produce logits.
kill: At 45 matched steps the loss over positions 0 to 63 is not at least 0.05 below the baseline's for the same bucket.

idea: Stream mixing as the exponential of a generator
mechanism: Rerepresent the residual as an ODE across depth: the 4-stream state flows under a transport generator, and the exact doubly stochastic step is exp(h L) with L a symmetric generator whose rows sum to zero. Replace the 20-iteration Sinkhorn projection of exp(logits) with a 4 x 4 matrix exponential of a softplus-parameterised symmetric generator with a learned step h per stage; this is exact, iteration-free, has clean gradients, and lets h act as a per-layer step size the optimizer can shrink or grow.
prediction: Parameter count unchanged in order (a few fewer logits per block); step time unchanged; residual RMS growth across depth flatter; validation loss within 0.005 of baseline, with the upside only if Sinkhorn's gradient noise was costing something.
test: A 45-step matched run comparing loss and the per-layer residual RMS profile; a check that each mixing matrix is doubly stochastic to 1e-6 at init and after 45 steps.
target: residual RMS growth; gradient norm spread
scope: validation loss at 1024, plus the two diagnostic cells as a secondary measure.
breaks: Stream mixing is produced by projecting exponentiated logits with 20 Sinkhorn iterations.
keeps: The 4-stream state, the read softmax, the write sigmoids, the identity-near init.
kill: At 45 matched steps the loss is more than 0.02 above the baseline's, or any mixing matrix departs from doubly stochastic by more than 1e-4.

mechanism: Attention is a kernel smoother whose bandwidth is fixed by QK-norm at one gain per channel shared by every token. A tiny Linear(384 to 6) with softplus gives each query its own temperature per head, so a token can retrieve sharply when it has a precise key and smooth when it does not.
prediction: Params rise by 27,648; step time unchanged; attention entropy in deep layers spreads (lower on retrieval heads, higher elsewhere); validation loss falls by about 0.005.
test: A 45-step matched run with per-layer attention entropy logged; falsified if entropy variance across queries does not widen or loss does not drop.

idea: Cross-layer latent KV sharing, parameters reinvested in depth
mechanism: Pairs of adjacent layers share compress, latent norm and expand (the latent is already normalised, so a second layer can read it), saving about 2.07M parameters; spend them on a 13th block, which the compute headroom covers.
prediction: Non-embedding params land near 21.0M (under cap); step time rises by about 7 percent; validation loss falls by 0.005 to 0.01 if a shared latent costs less than a block gains.
test: Build-only for the count; a 45-step matched run against the baseline and against a 13-layer unshared model to separate the two effects.

idea: Diagonal gear ratio on the tied head
mechanism: Input and output share one vector per token, yet reading wants a unit-scale geometry and writing wants a logit-scale one; a learned per-dimension scale between the final norm and the tied head lets them differ at a cost of 384 parameters.
prediction: Params rise by 384; step time unchanged; validation loss falls by 0.002 to 0.005, with most of the gain on rare tokens whose embeddings are rarely updated from the input side.
test: A 45-step matched run; falsified if the scale stays within 2 percent of one and loss does not move. Range worth sweeping: init 1.0 versus the final-norm gain removed.

idea: Time-matched budget with a factored head
mechanism: The head is 42 percent of forward compute and is the one block whose cost buys no representational depth; a two-level softmax over 224 frequency bands times 224 members computes 448 dot products per token instead of 50304, so at equal wall-clock the model sees about 1.5x the tokens. The full 50304-way logits needed by the exam are recovered exactly as band log-prob plus member log-prob, computed only at exam time.
prediction: Step time about 0.6x the baseline and peak VRAM about 0.5 GB lower because no (B*T, 50304) logits tensor exists in training; parameters +86k for the band matrix. At the fixed token budget the factorization costs +0.02 to +0.04 nats; at the baseline's wall-clock the extra tokens are worth about -0.05
test: A 3-step timing run must show under 3.0s per step, then a 45-step time-matched comparison. New success measure: validation loss after the baseline's measured wall-clock for 50M tokens on the same card, three seeds, same Welch test.
scope: validation loss at 1024 under a time-matched verifier; under the current token-matched exam it is a loss
breaks: the budget is counted in tokens processed, so any compute per token up to 2x is free.
keeps: the same backbone, data, optimizer, schedule and exam windows; only the head factorization and the budget's unit change.
kill: at 45 matched steps the factored model's train loss is more than 0.08 nats above the baseline's, which means the factorization itself, not the speed, is what moved.

idea: Exam after one step of adaptation, model trained to adapt
mechanism: The exam scores tokens 513 to 1024 of each window after one SGD step on the window's own first 512 tokens, adapting only the 9,600 RMSNorm gains; training runs the same inner step on every micro-batch and backpropagates the second-half loss through the adapted gains first-order, so the gains become a channel the model learns to steer from 512 tokens of in-domain text. The frozen first-half loss is kept in the training sum so the unadapted model stays comparable.
prediction: Step time about 1.5x; parameters unchanged; frozen validation loss within 0.005 of the baseline; adapted second-half loss 0.03 to 0.08 nats below the frozen second-half loss, since dynamic evaluation gains are largest for small models.
test: A 45-step run that logs three numbers per step: first-half loss, frozen second-half loss, adapted second-half loss. New success measure: mean adapted loss on positions 513 to 1024 over the same 2M validation tokens, three seeds, with the frozen loss reported beside it.
source: own; the exam side builds on dynamic evaluation, https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.07432
scope: validation loss at 1024 under an adaptation verifier; also what the model can learn at inference
breaks: the exam scores the saved weights frozen, one forward pass per window, no state carried in or out.
keeps: the architecture, optimizer, data and token budget; the inner step touches only norm gains, so the frozen model remains a drop-in GPT.
kill: at 45 matched steps the adapted second-half train loss is not at least 0.01 nats below the frozen second-half loss, or the frozen loss is more than 0.05 above the baseline.

mechanism: About a quarter of the training signal comes from positions with under 256 tokens of context, where the loss is 0.3 to 0.5 nats higher and mostly irreducible by a 21M model; masking the loss on positions 0 to 255 and keeping them as context shifts every gradient toward mechanisms that use context, such as induction and long-range copying. The exam then scores positions 513 to 1024 only, treating the model as a conditional predictor rather than a window scorer.
prediction: Step time and parameters unchanged; loss at positions 0 to 255 rises by about 0.05; loss at positions 512 and later falls by about 0.01; the uniform exam moves by +0.005 or less, the late-position exam by -0.01.
test: A 45-step run reporting the loss split into position bands 0-255, 256-511, 512-1023 for the candidate and the baseline. New success measure: mean validation loss on positions 513 to 1024 of the fixed windows, three seeds.
scope: validation loss at 1024 under a late-position verifier; under the uniform exam it is neutral at best
breaks: the objective and the exam weight every position of every window equally.
keeps: next-token cross entropy, the same model, data, optimizer and budget; only which positions contribute to the loss changes.
kill: at 45 matched steps the candidate's train loss on positions 512 and later is not at least 0.01 nats below the baseline's on the same band.

mechanism: The input stays GPT-2 tokens for cheap context, but the output becomes the next token's byte string, produced by a two-layer byte decoder of width 192 conditioned on the final hidden state and teacher-forced for about five byte steps per position. The 50304-way head and its 42 percent of compute disappear, rare tokens share statistics through their spellings, and every GPT-2 token is a unique prefix-free byte string plus end marker, so token probability is the product of byte probabilities and the measure becomes bits per byte.
prediction: Head compute drops to about 5 percent; the byte decoder adds about 1.0M non-embedding parameters, within the cap; training peak VRAM falls by about 0.4 GB. Token-equivalent loss within 0.05 of the baseline at 50M tokens, with the largest change on rare tokens; at matched time the freed compute pays
test: A 45-step run reporting byte NLL summed per token and averaged per position next to the baseline's token CE; a 3-step timing run. New success measure: bits per byte on the 2M validation tokens' underlying bytes, three seeds.
source: own; the measurement unit follows byte-level work such as https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871
scope: bits per byte at 1024 under a byte verifier; the current exam cannot score it directly without enumerating all 50304 spe
breaks: the unit of modeling and of measurement is the GPT-2 token, and the tokenizer is fixed.
keeps: the token embedding, the whole backbone, the optimizer, data and budget; only the head and the measure change.
kill: at 45 matched steps the per-token byte NLL is more than 0.15 nats above the baseline's token CE.

mechanism: Random windows and the fixed exam windows both cut across documents, so most windows contain one boundary and the model learns to discount a foreign prefix and parks junk in the first-token sink. Building a block-diagonal causal mask from the end-of-text token inside forward, and restarting rotary positions at each boundary, removes that cost and makes in-document position exact; this uses only the input ids and is legal under the current exam.
prediction: Step time +5 to +10 percent because the masked path leaves the flash kernel; parameters unchanged; validation loss -0.005 to -0.015, with the gain concentrated at positions 256 and later within a document and none at document starts.
test: A 3-step timing and peak-memory check first, since the mask costs a few MB and headroom is 0.1 GB; then 45 matched steps. Proposed companion measure for a new verifier: validation loss stratified by in-document position bands 0-15, 16-63, 64-255, 256+, so the context-use slope becomes visible.
target: loss at late positions, downward; first-token attention mass, downward

idea: Exact causal pointer cache in the head
mechanism: Add one extra attention head whose weights over earlier positions are read as a copy distribution over the tokens that followed those positions, and mix it with the softmax head through a learned sigmoid gate on the final hidden state. During training the mixture probability of the target needs only a (B, T, T) match matrix of equal next-tokens, so no vocabulary-sized tensor is ever built; at exam time forward builds the full log-mixture logits once in no-grad, which the exam's cross entropy consumes unchanged.
prediction: Parameters +0.3M for the pointer query and key projections and the gate; step time +3 percent; training peak VRAM unchanged; validation loss -0.01 to -0.02, almost all of it on tokens that already appeared in the window.
test: Check that the exam-time logits path fits in memory at micro-batch 4, then 45 matched steps with the loss split into tokens seen earlier in the window and tokens not seen.

idea: Make the four streams actually differ
mechanism: At init the mixing diagonal is exp(6) to 1, so each stream keeps 99.3 percent of itself, and the write weights are 1.015 on the own stream and 0.995 on the others, so every branch writes almost equally into four streams that start as identical copies; the residual expansion costs four times the stream memory for a near-null operation, and AdamW's decay pulls the mixing toward uniform, which averages the streams back together. Setting the write logits to +2.0 on the own stream and -2.0 elsewhere makes attention write mainly into stream 0 and the MLP into stream 1, leaving streams 2 and 3 as nea
prediction: Parameters and step time unchanged; residual RMS grows more slowly in the carry streams and the read logits move further from uniform by the end; validation loss -0.003 to -0.01.
test: 45 matched steps against the baseline; sweep own-stream logit in {1.0, 2.0, 3.0} and other-stream logit in {-1.0, -2.0, -3.0}, and log the per-stream RMS at layer 12.
target: residual RMS growth, downward; validation loss
